samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small block drawn with a thick black frame, and every pale grey mark lying outside that frame is inert decoration that means nothing. Inside the frame are nine equal square pits in three rows of three, each pit filled with its own solid floor colour, and no two pits share a colour. The nine pits are ordered by reading order: left to right along the top row, then left to right along the middle row, then left to right along the bottom row, and after the last pit the order wraps round to the first pit again. Each pit holds nought, one, two or three pips, drawn as equal small black squares standing in a row on that pit's floor; a pit with no black square on it is empty. Exactly one pit carries a thick white ring drawn just inside its own border; the ring is only a marking, it never moves, and the pit it rings holds pips and a floor colour like any other pit. Now sow the pips. Lift every pip out of the ringed pit, leaving that pit empty, and hold them in your hand. Drop them one at a time into the pits that follow in reading order, one single pip into each successive pit, wrapping past the last pit back to the first, until your hand is empty. Then look at the pit that received the very last pip of the handful. If that pit had been empty just before that pip landed, so it now holds exactly one pip, the sowing stops there. Otherwise that pit now holds more than one pip: lift every pip out of it, including the one that just landed, leaving it empty, and sow that new handful onward in exactly the same way, continuing from the pit that follows it. Repeat this until a handful ends in a pit that was empty before the final pip landed, and that pit is where the sowing stops. What is the floor colour of the pit where the sowing finally stops? Answer with one of red, green, blue, yellow, orange, purple, teal, pink or brown.
